sections.title: MODELS: every saved final model is loaded and scored on the 647 test windows

items.claim: The saved preprocessor equals one re-fitted from the training rows
evidence: medians, scales and the 128 output columns identical: True

items.claim: Decision metrics recomputed from the loaded models equal test_metrics.csv within 1e-06 for all 36 models (accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro-F1, per-class precision / recall / F1, Normal recall; argmax and saved-threshold decisions; all test windows, SN and TT)
evidence: model                          BA recomputed  BA in file  max diff decision  max diff ranking    BA 95% CI
95% CI = block bootstrap (1000 resamples) from test_bootstrap_ci.csv; 'decision' = metrics computed from the predicted class; 'ranking' = ROC-AUC / PR-AUC

items.claim: Ranking metrics (ROC-AUC / PR-AUC) reproduce; differences above 1e-6 are explained by tied scores
evidence: ranking metrics (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, PR-AUC of Normal) equal the file within 1e-06 for 33 of 36 models
model                 max diff vs file  spread from 1e-15 noise  distinct scores

the recomputed probabilities of these models equal the original ones to ~1e-16, but forest scores are multiples of 1/(number of trees): many are EXACTLY tied, and a 1e-16 change in floating-point summation

order between runs re-orders the ties, which moves AUC by the amount shown. Adding 1e-15 relative noise to the scores moves the AUC by a spread of the same size ('spread from 1e-15 noise'), so this is tie sensitivity, not a model difference.
decision metrics are not affected (they match to 1e-6 above)
